newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin says he wants professional Russian army.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says he wants professional Russian army.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin confirmed on Friday his intention to create a professional, non-conscript army in Russia but did not say anything about the fate of Defence Minister Igor Rodionov, whose position appears shaky.
"The task awaiting us is a transition to a professional army," the 66-year-old Kremlin leader said in a brief radio address. "Russia will have a professional army."
"Only this will enable us to maintain the combat ability of the armed forces and the potential for nuclear deterrence in the 21st century," he said.
Yeltsin has ordered the creation of a professional army instead of the current force based on teenage conscription by the year 2000.
But both Rodionov and Kremlin defence aide Yuri Baturin, who disagree over other aspect of military reforms, are united at least in saying the task is unrealistic.
Rodionov is campaigning bitterly and publicly for more funding for the army, saying the situation there is catastrophic and no reform is possible without additional money.
Baturin says reforms should be implemented within the funding the state can afford.
Yeltsin rebuked Rodionov on Wednesday, telling him through a press statement to stop "whining' and get down to the task of reforming the army.
The remark triggered strong speculation in the Russian media that Rodionov was about to be dismissed.
But Yeltsin did not address the issue in his radio speech, reiterating only the neeed to launch reforms.
"I know that we have to start reforms in very difficult conditions," he said. "But we must start. It is the only way to revive the armed forces of the country, their combat ability and their glory."
